PR #256 final round at d94fa60ff4a214f6101987a64939e1e361d17c85:
PASS-WITH-NOTES, R256-001 closed. Independent saved-row aggregation and
performance's committed audit agree: guard clear/cold 970->710 (large
265->5), warm stopped 4->56, refusals124->124, warnings0->312 for Warn.
Those are guard outcomes, not cache-state estimates. Warn leaves 265
actually-cold large sends allowed (260 warned); claim no token savings.

C34 follow-up R256-N1, accepted by coder: audit.py:279-280 still calls
the fixed-hour old_warm heuristic cache_old_*. Rename heuristic pair;
derive actual old CACHE metrics from old_cache with unknowns excluded.
Actual old CACHE counts are37/179 among8975known,427unknown, not785/33.
This secondary pair is not used by guard_* or policy replay. Do not
reopen a third review round for it.

All policy values retain strict >60m ceiling. Known-TTL refusal is
inclusive at the configured 100/150/200 percent; Warn allows with a
warning after TTL. At exactly60m, Warn still warns if TTL elapsed,
while RefuseAt depends on its threshold. Idle nudge still allows only
Clear|Busy; Warn spares it. FYI/revive positive-evidence logic unchanged.

Successful CI attempt2 at exact head: run44460835051, job135348751127,
JUnit artifact14500715194. 2551passing JUnit cases; two new Python-audit
Vitest regressions passed. No local builds/tests or duplicate fleet scan.

IMPORTANT OWNERSHIP SUPERSESSION: the round-2 PM packet assigns the
after-deploy f214-audit-after to PERFORMANCE ONLY. This overrides the
reviewer-owned obligation in the R1 memory and verdict. Reviewer and
security DO NOT run it. Performance audits after >=3days of deployment.
